source: NCERT Class VIII, Curiosity: Textbook of Science, Ch. 8.

sections.heading: 1. Elements
points: An **element** = a **pure substance** made of only **one kind of atom**; it cannot be broken into simpler substances by chemical means.
There are about **118 known elements** (e.g. hydrogen, oxygen, carbon, iron, gold).
Each element has a **symbol** (H, O, C, Fe, Au); grouped as **metals, non-metals and metalloids**.

sections.heading: 2. Compounds
points: A **compound** = a pure substance formed when **two or more elements combine chemically** in a **fixed ratio**.
Its properties are **different** from those of its elements (e.g. **water = H₂O** from hydrogen + oxygen; **common salt = NaCl** from sodium + chlorine).
A compound can be separated only by **chemical methods**, not physical ones.

sections.heading: 3. Mixtures
points: A **mixture** = two or more substances **mixed physically** in **any ratio**, keeping their **own properties**.

sub: **Heterogeneous** — not uniform (e.g. sand + iron filings, oil + water).

points: Mixtures can be separated by **physical methods** (filtration, evaporation, magnet, etc.).

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Element = one kind of atom (H, O, Fe); ~118 known; metals/non-metals/metalloids.
Compound = elements chemically combined in a fixed ratio (water H₂O, salt NaCl); new properties.
Mixture = substances mixed physically in any ratio; keep their properties.
Homogeneous (uniform, e.g. air) vs heterogeneous (non-uniform) mixtures.
Compounds separated by chemical means; mixtures by physical means.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: A **compound** has a **fixed ratio** and **new properties**; a **mixture** has **any ratio** and keeps original properties.
**Compounds** are separated by **chemical** methods; **mixtures** by **physical** methods.
An **element** cannot be broken into simpler substances chemically.
